[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **step-by-step recipe** that turns the empty “page-background” you see above the horizon into a proper sky with a gentle haze (fog) that blends into the terrain.  
All of the pieces are native MapLibre GL JS – no extra plugins are required.

---

## 1️⃣  Prerequisites (you already have these)

```js
// 1️⃣  Create the map
const map = new maplibregl.Map({
  container: 'map',
  style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json',   // any style you like
  center: [13.4, 52.5],   // lon/lat
  zoom: 12,
  pitch: 70,              // you already set this
  bearing: 0,
  antialias: true        // important for smooth terrain rendering
});

// 2️⃣  Add the DEM source (raster-dem) and enable terrain
map.addSource('terrain-dem', {
  type: 'raster-dem',
  url: 'https://tiles.mapterhorn.com/tilejson.json', // ← your DEM tileset
  tileSize: 256,
  maxzoom: 12
});

map.setTerrain({ source: 'terrain-dem', exaggeration: 1 });
```

If you can already see the 3-D relief, the code above is working.

---

## 2️⃣  Add a **sky** object

The sky is **not a layer** – it lives at the root of the style (or can be added later with `map.setSky`).  
When a sky object is present, MapLibre draws it **behind every layer** (including the background layer).  
If you have a background layer that is fully opaque (`background-color: #fff`), it will hide the sky.
Either remove that background layer or make it transparent.

### 2️⃣-A.  Quick-and-dirty “default sky”

```js
map.on('load', () => {
  // This adds the sky with the default “atmosphere” look.
  map.setSky({
    'sky-color': '#199EF3',          // deep blue at zenith
    'sky-horizon-blend': 0.5,        // how quickly the blue fades to horizon
    'horizon-color': '#ffffff',      // near-white at the horizon line
    'horizon-fog-blend': 0.5,        // blend horizon → fog
    'fog-color': '#cceeff',          // light blue-gray haze that meets the ground
    'fog-ground-blend': 0.5          // how far the fog reaches down the terrain
  });
});
```

That’s enough to see a blue sky, a bright horizon, and a faint haze that follows the terrain.

### 2️⃣-B.  A more “cinematic” sky (optional tweaks)

| Property | What it does | Typical values |
|----------|--------------|----------------|
| `sky-color` | Color of the sky at the zenith (top of the view) | `'#87CEEB'` (light sky-blue) |
| `sky-horizon-blend` | How quickly the zenith color fades to the horizon color (0 = instant, 1 = slow) | `0.3 – 0.6` |
| `horizon-color` | Color of the sky right at the horizon line | `'#F8F8FF'` (almost white) |
| `horizon-fog-blend` | Blend between horizon color and fog color | `0.4 – 0.7` |
| `fog-color` | Colour of the atmospheric haze that meets the ground | `'#B0C4DE'` (steel-blue) |
| `fog-ground-blend` | How far the fog reaches down the terrain (0 = only at the very edge, 1 = covers the whole view) | `0.5 – 0.8` |

```js
map.on('load', () => {
  map.setSky({
    'sky-color': '#87CEEB',
    'sky-horizon-blend': 0.4,
    'horizon-color': '#F8F8FF',
    'horizon-fog-blend': 0.55,
    'fog-color': '#B0C4DE',
    'fog-ground-blend': 0.65
  });
});
```

Feel free to experiment – the sky is rendered in the GPU, so changes are instant.

---

## 3️⃣  Make sure the **background layer** does not hide the sky

If your style contains a `background` layer (most starter styles do), it will paint over the sky unless its opacity is < 1.

```js
// Example: make the background semi-transparent
map.setPaintProperty('background', 'background-color', 'rgba(255,255,255,0)');
// or simply remove it:
map.removeLayer('background');
```

> **Tip:** The sky is drawn *after* the background, but before all other layers.  
> If you keep a background layer, set its opacity to `0` (transparent) or a very light colour that you actually want to see.

---

## 4️⃣  Verify it works

1. **Pitch the map** (you already have `pitch: 70`).  
2. **Look above the horizon** – you should now see a gradient from the zenith colour down to the horizon colour, then a soft fog that follows the terrain.  
3. **Rotate the map** – the sky stays fixed (it does not rotate with the map) because it is a world-space effect, not a layer.

If you still see the plain page background:

| Possible cause | Fix |
|----------------|-----|
| `map.setSky` was called **before** the map finished loading. | Call it inside `map.on('load', …)` (as shown). |
| A `background` layer with opaque colour is on top. | Remove it or set its opacity to `0`. |
| Using an old MapLibre version (< 5.5). | Upgrade to the latest 5.x release – sky was added in 5.5. |
| The style’s `sky` object is overridden by a later `setStyle`. | Add the sky *after* any `setStyle` call, or include it in the style JSON itself. |

---

## 5️⃣  (Optional) Put the sky directly into the **style JSON**

If you prefer to ship the sky with the style rather than call `setSky` at runtime, add a top-level `sky` object:

```json
{
  "version": 8,
  "sources": { … },
  "layers": [ … ],
  "terrain": { "source": "terrain-dem", "exaggeration": 1 },
  "sky": {
    "sky-color": "#87CEEB",
    "sky-horizon-blend": 0.4,
    "horizon-color": "#F8F8FF",
    "horizon-fog-blend": 0.55,
    "fog-color": "#B0C4DE",
    "fog-ground-blend": 0.65
  }
}
```

When the style loads, the sky appears automatically – no extra JavaScript needed.

---

## 🎉  Recap – What you need to do

1. **Enable terrain** (`map.setTerrain` – you already have this).  
2. **Pitch the camera** (`pitch > 0`).  
3. **Add a sky object** (via `map.setSky` *or* in the style JSON).  
4. **Make the background transparent or remove it** so the sky can be seen.  

That’s it! Your map will now show a realistic sky with a gentle haze that meets the ground, instead of the flat page background. Happy mapping! 🚀
